title: 1.4. Practice Lab: print() Formatting & Escape Sequences
summary: Hands-on Cisco NetAcad lab: Practice using escape sequences (\n, \t, \\, \") to build formatted multi-line ASCII art and formatted console banners.
learningObjectives: Use backslash escape sequences to embed special characters in strings.
Construct multi-line formatted console outputs without invoking dozens of individual print() calls.
Troubleshoot syntax errors resulting from unescaped quotation marks.

sections.heading: 1.4.1 Escape Sequences in Python Strings
sections.content:
An escape sequence is a special combination of characters that begins with a backslash (\), followed by a letter or symbol:

• \n : Newline — shifts execution to the beginning of the next line.
• \t : Horizontal Tab — advances output to the next tab stop.
• \\ : Literal Backslash — renders a single backslash character.
• \" : Literal Double Quote — includes a double quotation mark inside a double-quoted string without terminating it.
• \' : Literal Single Quote — includes a single quotation mark inside a single-quoted string.

codeExamples.code:
print("First line\nSecond line\n\tIndented third line")
print("The teacher said: \"Escape characters are essential.\"")
codeExamples.explanation: Escape sequences allow precise formatting of text and quotation nesting within string literals.
codeExamples.expectedOutput:
First line
Second line
	Indented third line
The teacher said: "Escape characters are essential."

exercises.title: NetAcad Lab: The print() Arrow Generator
exercises.objective: Write a program using print() formatting and escape sequences to generate a clean ASCII arrow pointing upwards.
exercises.description: Recreate the iconic Cisco NetAcad print arrow lab using optimal print statements.
instructions: Print an ASCII arrow pointing up using asterisks (*).
Ensure lines are centered and proportional.
Use escape sequences to minimize redundant code.
hints: You can duplicate asterisks or use multiple arguments with sep=' '.
exercises.submissionRequirements: Submit code that prints both statements without syntax errors.
exercises.solutionExplanation:
print('    *')
print('   * *')
print('  *   *')
print(' *     *')
print('***   ***')
print('  *   *')
print('  *   *')
print('  *****')

recap: Escape sequences provide granular control over text layout, indentation, and special character representation.
